title: GLM-5.2 — research dossier (external model, NOT a hexa-codex component)
name: GLM-5.2
summary: Z.ai (Zhipu AI) flagship open-weights LLM. ~744-753B-param Mixture-of-Experts (~40B active/token), native 1M-token context via IndexShare sparse-attention, MIT-licensed weights on HuggingFace/ModelScope, text-only. Released 2026-06-13 (coding-plan day-one) / 2026-06-16 (full open weights + API + benchmarks). #1 open-weights on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1 (51); top open-weight on the agentic-coding benches Z.ai reports (SWE-bench Pro 62.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1 81.0); beats GPT-5.5 on those at ~1/6th output-token cost; still trails Claude Opus 4.8 across the board and cedes competitive-coding (LiveCodeBench/Codeforces/SWE-bench Verified) to DeepSeek V4 Pro.
note: This is a scratch research artifact (docs scratchDir = state/scratch/). It is a SNAPSHOT of public reporting as gathered 2026-06-22 via web research, NOT a hexa-codex architecture node. Every leaf is source-attributed; cross-source disagreements are flagged in `disputes`. Do NOT promote into ARCHITECTURE.json (external model ≠ project design, governance c4).

meta.vendor: Z.ai / Zhipu AI (Tsinghua-origin, founded 2019; HK IPO 2026-01-08, 2513.HK, ~US$6.6-7B val)
meta.license: MIT (weights only; training code/data NOT released → open-weight, not fully open-source)
meta.modality: text-only (vision handled by separate non-open GLM-5V-Turbo family)

children.name: architecture
children.summary: Sparse MoE on an MLA + DeepSeek-Sparse-Attention backbone (carried from GLM-5/5.1); the principal 5.2 delta is IndexShare.

children.name: moe-config
children.summary: From HF config.json (most authoritative): num_hidden_layers=78, hidden_size=6144, num_attention_heads=64, num_key_value_heads=64, head_dim=192, n_routed_experts=256, num_experts_per_tok=8, n_shared_experts=1, moe_intermediate_size=2048, first_k_dense_replace=3 (first 3 layers dense), num_nextn_predict_layers=1 (MTP), vocab_size=154880.

children.name: params
children.summary: Total ~744B (DISPUTED: 743B per vLLM recipe / 753B per HF card+Artificial Analysis / 744B per most resellers). Active per token ~39-40B. Memory is governed by FULL count (all experts resident); compute/latency closer to a dense ~40B model.

children.name: attention
children.summary: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) + DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA, from DeepSeek V3.2 lineage). DSA 'Lightning Indexer' selects a sparse top-k (reported top-2048) key set per query → attention cost near-linear in context.

children.name: indexshare
children.summary: HEADLINE 5.2 DELTA. Instead of recomputing the DSA top-k indexer at every layer, the full indexer runs once every 4 layers and the next 3 layers REUSE the indices. Claimed ~2.9x fewer per-token FLOPs at 1M context — what makes the 1M window practical. Paper: 'IndexCache: Accelerating Sparse Attention via Cross-Layer Index Reuse' (arXiv:2603.12201, arXiv ID extracted from card, not independently confirmed).

children.name: context-window
children.summary: Native 1,048,576 tokens (max_position_embeddings, trained not interpolated). rope_theta=8,000,000; rope_scaling NOT set (1M achieved via large RoPE base + sparse-attn training, inferred from config). Max output ~131,072 (128K). MTP=1 layer for EAGLE-style speculative decode (~+20% acceptance vs 5.1; vLLM extends to 5 draft tokens).

children.name: training
children.summary: Pretraining ~28.5T tokens (stated for GLM-5 series; up from 23T for GLM-4.5). Post-training: agentic RL with critic-based PPO + an 'anti-hack' module against reward hacking on coding. Reasoning ('thinking') ON by default with effort levels High/Max (one reseller cites low/medium/max — unverified). Verbose: ~43K out tok/task, ~37K reasoning. Reportedly trained on Huawei chips without Nvidia (single-source, unverified).

children.name: vs-glm-5.1
children.summary: Context 200K→1M (~5x); max output ~64K→128K (~2x); per-layer DSA → IndexShare (2.9x fewer FLOPs @1M); MTP +~20% acceptance; SAME param scale (~744B/~40B) — gains from training, not scale; adds dual-effort reasoning + agentic-RL/critic-PPO/anti-hack.

children.name: benchmarks
children.summary: Source legend: [V]=vendor-claimed, [AA]=Artificial Analysis (independent), [3P]=other third-party. Z.ai selectively omits benches where DeepSeek V4 Pro leads.

children.name: coding
children.summary: [V] SWE-bench Pro 62.1 (GLM-5.1 58.4 / GPT-5.5 58.6 / Opus 4.8 69.2 / DeepSeek V4 Pro 55.4 / MiniMax-M3 59.0). [V] Terminal-Bench 2.1 81.0 (GPT-5.5 84 / Opus 4.8 85). [V] FrontierSWE 74.4 (GPT-5.5 72.6 / Opus 4.8 75.1). [V] MCP-Atlas ~76.8-77.0 (GPT-5.5 75.3 / Opus 4.8 77.8). NOT disclosed by Z.ai: SWE-bench Verified, LiveCodeBench, Codeforces — exactly where DeepSeek V4 Pro wins (Verified 80.6 / LiveCodeBench 93.5 / Codeforces 3206).

children.name: general-intelligence
children.summary: [AA] Intelligence Index v4.1 = 51 → #1 open-weights (MiniMax-M3 44, DeepSeek V4 Pro 44, Kimi K2.6 43); +11 over GLM-5.1; on the intelligence-vs-cost Pareto frontier. Caveat: token-hungry (43K out/task vs 24-37K peers) inflates real latency/cost. GDPval-AA v2 1524 (> GPT-5.5 1514).

children.name: reasoning-math
children.summary: [V] AIME 2026 99.2 (top of pack; GPT-5.5 98.3 / Gemini 3.1 Pro 98.2 / Opus 4.8 95.7). [V]/[AA] GPQA Diamond 91.2 (89 on AA harness; GPT-5.5 93.6 / Opus 4.8 93.6 / Gemini 3.1 Pro 94.3). [V] HLE no-tools 40.5 / with-tools 54.7. [AA] CritPt 21 (+16 vs 5.1). Trails closed frontier ~5-10pts on HLE/GPQA.

children.name: long-context
children.summary: [3P] Needle-in-haystack 3/3 at ~983K tokens (Phala). [AA] AA-LCR long-context reasoning 71% official (+9 vs 5.1 ~62%); a W4AFP8 serving run measured 76.0.

children.name: agentic-tooluse
children.summary: [V] MCP-Atlas 76.8-77.0 (≈ GPT-5.5 75.3, Opus 4.8 77.8). [AA] tau3-banking 27 (+15 vs 5.1, low absolute — weak spot). [3P] BFCL ~84%. Tool-Decathlon: behind Opus 4.8 & GPT-5.5. Relative weakness on multi-turn agent tasks.

children.name: vibe-reception
children.summary: Simon Willison: 'probably the most powerful text-only open-weights LLM.' #2 on Code Arena WebDev (behind Claude Fable 5) despite text-only. Strong animated-SVG gen. Knocks: token-hungry; SOME creative-output regressions vs GLM-5.1; heavy local hosting. ~91% positive sentiment tracker.

children.name: self-hosting
children.summary: Memory governed by full ~744B param count (no MoE memory saving); compute by ~40B active. Use EXPERT parallelism (vLLM --enable-expert-parallel / SGLang --enable-moe-ep), not plain TP.

children.name: repos
children.summary: zai-org/GLM-5.2 (BF16 main, ~1.5TB) · zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 (production-recommended, ~744-750GB) · unsloth/GLM-5.2-GGUF (1-bit→BF16 ladder) · pipenetwork/GLM-5.2-MLX-mixed-3_6bit (Apple Silicon, ~360GB). No separate base/instruct split — released model is instruct/chat. 44 quantized derivatives + 9 finetunes listed.

children.name: gpu-rigs
children.summary: FP8 production floor = 8x H200 (141GB → 1.13TB aggregate, headroom for KV); Z.ai docs cite 8x H100 baseline (640GB tight vs ~744GB weights → needs aggressive KV/offload). BF16 = 16x H100 or 8x H200+offload. KV cache ~25GB@256K FP8, x4 @1M → FP8 KV cache mandatory at 1M. Q4 GGUF ~376GB = 4x H100 / 2x H200.

children.name: engines
children.summary: Transformers≥0.5.12 · vLLM≥0.23.0 · SGLang≥0.5.13.post1 · KTransformers≥0.5.12 (CPU/GPU hybrid) · Unsloth≥0.1.47-beta · llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio/Jan (GGUF) · MLX (Apple) · Ascend NPU. FP8 ≈ near-lossless vs BF16 (production sweet spot); Q4_K_M = local quality/size knee; 1-2-bit = 'can it run at all' tier.

children.name: consumer-feasibility
children.summary: NOT runnable on single 24-48GB GPU alone, NOT on ≤128GB Mac. Realistic single-box floor = 256GB Mac Studio (UD-IQ2_XXS 2-bit @ ~3-9 tok/s) OR 24GB-GPU + 256GB-RAM workstation (llama.cpp/KTransformers MoE offload, single-digit tok/s). 192GB Mac marginal (<1 tok/s). 512GB Mac → MLX 3.6-bit (~360GB) higher quality.

children.name: business-ecosystem
children.summary: Pricing, license terms, availability timeline, integrations, company, and controversy.

children.name: pricing-api
children.summary: Direct (Z.ai/Fireworks): $1.40/M input, $4.40/M output (Fireworks cached input $0.26/M, -80%). OpenRouter shows rounded $1/$4. 'vs GPT-5.5 $5/$30 → ~1/6th output cost' (output is dominant cost driver; directionally accurate, NOT all-in TCO). One 18-task hands-on: $2.74 GLM-5.2 vs $16.10 GPT-5.5.

children.name: pricing-coding-plan
children.summary: Tiers Lite $10 / Pro $30 / Max $80 per independent trackers (Z.ai docs say only 'from ~$18/mo' — DISCREPANCY flagged). Approx weekly caps Lite 400 / Pro 2000 / Max 8000 prompts; all include GLM-5.2 + 1M context. CAVEAT: GLM-5.2 quota-intensive — 3x deduction peak (14-18 UTC+8), 2x off-peak (1x promo through end-Sep). Plan restricted to officially supported tools.

children.name: license-terms
children.summary: MIT on weights: commercial use, modify, redistribute, fine-tune, self-host, embed in closed products — no royalties, no acceptable-use clause. NO regional restrictions (HF + ModelScope). Caveat: MIT covers weights only — does NOT shield API traffic from China data law.

children.name: timeline
children.summary: 2026-06-13: day-one on all Coding Plan tiers (1M ctx), NO benchmarks at launch. 2026-06-16 (~'following week', +3 days): standalone API + Z.ai chatbot + MIT open weights (HF/ModelScope) + full benchmark scorecard.

children.name: integrations
children.summary: First-party endpoint is Anthropic Messages API-compatible (base-URL + model swap). Day-one 8-agent set: Claude Code, Cline, OpenCode, Roo Code, Goose, Crush, OpenClaw, Kilo Code (Claude Code recommends GLM-5.2 for both Opus+Sonnet slots, GLM-4.5-air for Haiku). Cursor NOT official (custom config only). Day-zero hosts: Fireworks, Together, Novita, DeepInfra, HF Inference Providers, OpenRouter. Tool-calling schema endpoint-dependent (OpenAI-style vs Anthropic tool-use).

children.name: company
children.summary: Zhipu AI / Z.ai, founded 2019 (Tang Jie & Li Juanzi, Tsinghua). HK IPO 2026-01-08 (2513.HK), HK$116.20/share, raised ~HK$4.17B (~US$560M), retail oversubscribed >1000x, val ~US$6.6-7B (~70% proceeds → model R&D to 2028). Pre-IPO ~US$1.5B (Alibaba, Tencent, Ant, Meituan, Xiaomi, Hillhouse, Qiming, Aramco Prosperity7). 2025 revenue +132% YoY.

children.name: controversy
children.summary: (1) No benchmarks at launch → 'where are the benchmarks?' pushback (resolved +3 days). (2) 'Benchmaxxing'/fade skepticism. (3) 'Open but paywalled' first days. (4) China data risk: API routes through Z.ai infra subject to China National Intelligence Law regardless of location — MIT license does NOT shield API traffic; self-host in EU for GDPR. (5) May-2025 Zhipu app flagged for over-collection; May-2026 US House inquiry named Zhipu. (6) Absent from Anthropic Feb-2026 distillation accusations.

children.summary: FORECAST ONLY (not shipped): Z.ai signaled (roadmap screenshot via AINews/Latent.Space) intent to release an open-weight model matching Anthropic Fable-class capability by end of 2026. Stated ambition, not a commitment.

children.name: param-count
children.summary: 743B (vLLM) vs 744B (resellers) vs 753B (HF card + Artificial Analysis). Active ~39-40B. No canonical technical-report figure.

children.name: max-output
children.summary: 128,000 vs 131,072 both cited.

children.name: reasoning-effort-labels

children.name: coding-plan-price
children.summary: $10/$30/$80 (trackers) vs 'from ~$18/mo' (Z.ai docs); prompt caps 'approximate', vary by source.

children.name: arxiv-ids
children.summary: GLM-5 report arXiv:2602.15763 + IndexCache arXiv:2603.12201 extracted from card text, NOT independently confirmed to resolve.

children.name: training-hardware
children.summary: 'Huawei chips, no Nvidia' is single-source, unverified.

children.name: security-china-model
children.summary: The 'avoid Chinese models for security' fear targets the WRONG layer. Self-hosted open weights cannot exfiltrate; the risk is the vendor API. Researched 2026-06-22.

children.name: weights-cannot-phone-home
children.summary: Central myth debunked: weights = inert .safetensors tensors (just numbers, no code, no syscalls, no network). LLM forward pass = pure linear algebra (output=f(weights,input)). A network-isolated/air-gapped self-host CANNOT send data anywhere regardless of who trained it. Distinguish 3 layers: WEIGHTS (inert) vs RUNTIME (vLLM/llama.cpp — open-source code YOU choose, can be egress-locked) vs API (vendor servers — the ONLY real exfiltration vector).

children.name: real-supply-chain-risks
children.summary: Vendor-INDEPENDENT (apply to US models too): (1) pickle RCE in .bin/.pt/.ckpt — torch.load runs arbitrary code; nullifAI (Feb 2025) shipped reverse-shells on HF bypassing Picklescan. (2) trust_remote_code=True custom modeling.py executes arbitrary Python (CVE-2026-4372 config-bypass). (3) tampered community quant re-uploads (unknown uploaders). (4) inference-stack CVEs. ALL mitigated by safetensors + trust_remote_code=False + official-org-only + patched stack.

children.name: glm-5.2-security-posture
children.summary: GLM ships safetensors (NOT pickle → no load-time RCE). config.json declares native glm4_moe arch with NO auto_map → loads with trust_remote_code=FALSE. MIT license = no legal blocker. (Always re-verify the exact repo's format at download.)

children.name: weight-baked-risks-survive-selfhost
children.summary: Self-host fixes data egress, NOT model behavior: (1) censorship/CCP bias is IN the weights (DeepSeek-R1 refuses Tiananmen even run locally via Groq) — a content/quality issue, not a breach, and the ONE thing you can patch since you hold the weights. (2) jailbreak fragility (NIST/CAISI: DeepSeek R1-0528 complied with 94% of malicious requests self-hosted vs 8% US ref) → output guardrails mandatory. (3) hidden weight-backdoor: DEMONSTRATED possible (Anthropic Sleeper Agents — insecure code on hidden trigger, survives fine-tuning) but NOT observed in GLM/DeepSeek/Qwen; origin-independent, mitigate by sandbox + reviewing generated code.

children.name: enterprise-policy-reality
children.summary: Bans almost ALL target DeepSeek's hosted API/app (US federal+17 states, Italy Garante/GDPR, Australia, Taiwan, S.Korea PIPC, India) — NOT the open weights, and NONE name a GLM/Zhipu usage ban. Zhipu's only exposure: BIS Entity List (restricts exporting US tech TO Zhipu, does NOT bar US using GLM) + Apr-2026 House inquiry (critical-infra scope). KEY PRECEDENT: Microsoft bans the DeepSeek APP for employees but HOSTS the model on Azure ('open-source, self-host = no data to China'). NIST/CAISI evaluated by downloading weights to its OWN cloud, not the API. GLM/DeepSeek/Qwen on AWS Bedrock/Azure/Vertex/Together/Fireworks (US-region hosting removes the China-data-transfer problem).

children.name: acceptable-vs-nogo
children.summary: ACCEPTABLE (non-regulated) with: self-host in isolated VPC + no-egress + safetensors/no-remote-code + official-org + output guardrails + RBAC/audit + MIT license review. HARD NO-GO regardless of hosting: federal/public-sector, ITAR/classified/defense, critical infrastructure, heavily-regulated PHI/PII. Compliance: GDPR → EU-region self-host; SOC2/ISO27001 audit YOUR deployment boundary not model nationality; framework NIST AI 600-1.

children.name: deployment-cost
children.summary: Inference cost is heavily usage-dependent (~100x spread). Self-hosting is for SOVEREIGNTY/SECURITY, not savings — savings only at very high sustained volume. GPU prices June 2026. Researched 2026-06-22.

children.name: options-monthly-24x7
children.summary: Third-party API: pay-per-use $1.40/$4.40 per 1M tok. GLM Coding Plan: $10-80/mo flat. Cloud 8xH200 FP8 self-host: on-demand ~$25,000/mo, spot ~$10,500/mo. Mac Studio 256GB (2-bit) one-time ~$8,000. On-prem 8xH200 server ~$250-400k capex (~$7-11k/mo amortized 3yr).

children.name: break-even
children.summary: Spot 8xH200 (~$10,500/mo fixed) = API at ~2.4B output tok/mo. Below that threshold API/Coding-Plan is cheaper (true for MOST teams). The 'self-host saves money' claim is usually wrong — self-host for data sovereignty, not cost.

children.name: intermittent-hourly
children.summary: Rent only when working (4h/day x 20d = 80h/mo): 8xH200 on-demand ~$35/h → ~$2,800/mo; spot ~$14.6/h → ~$1,170/mo. Best fit for experiments / security self-host without 24x7 cost.

children.name: quantization-cost-quality
children.summary: Fewer bits = fewer GPUs = lower cost, but quality drops. FP8 ~744GB=8xH200, 24x7 spot ~$10,500/mo, ≈lossless. Q4_K_M ~400GB=4xH200/6xH100, spot ~$5,300/mo, practical knee (CODING FLOOR). 2-bit ~238GB=2xH200, spot ~$2,600/mo, noticeable drop. 1-bit ~180GB, ~$1,300/mo, 'runs at all' tier. Q4 is the lowest bit-depth that keeps coding accuracy; below it trades quality for cost.

children.name: customization-finetune-vs-rag
children.summary: Adapting GLM to your data: pretraining is done by Zhipu (open-weight value). For company data, RAG usually beats fine-tuning. Researched 2026-06-22.

children.name: training-cost-tiers
children.summary: Pretraining-from-scratch = millions of $ (Zhipu already did it; the open-weight payoff). Full fine-tune 744B = optimizer+gradient blows memory 3-4x inference → dozens of GPUs, very expensive, rarely done. QLoRA (quantized base frozen + small adapter) = the de-facto standard, ~hundreds-to-thousands of $ per run.

children.name: qlora-cost
children.summary: TRAP: even LoRA must hold the FULL base in memory (needed for fwd/bwd) → 'inference hardware floor + a bit' = ~8xH200 one node at 4-bit base. 1 run = hours to 2-3 days. Cloud on-demand ~$840/day, multi-day $2-3k; spot ~halve. Real cost = experiment iterations (3-10x) x data prep, not one run. Cheaper path: managed fine-tune APIs (Together/Fireworks) — upload dataset, tens-to-hundreds of $ (confirm GLM support per host). Unsloth supports GLM QLoRA officially.

children.name: rag-vs-finetune-decision
children.summary: DECISION RULE for internal DB/wiki: use RAG (retrieval), NOT fine-tuning. RAG (open-book): retrieves relevant docs and feeds them to GLM at query time. Use RAG when → facts/documents, frequently updated, citations needed, reduce hallucination (internal wiki/DB = almost always RAG). Use fine-tune when → company tone/format/behavior, internal jargon (static, not facts). Both → RAG + thin QLoRA on top.

children.name: rag-cost-and-security
children.summary: RAG is strikingly cheap: embedding (one-time index of whole wiki) = tens of $; vector DB (Qdrant/pgvector) self-host free-to-cheap; doc updates = re-embed only changed docs (~free); GLM inference cost unchanged. vs fine-tune (hundreds-thousands $ + re-train when docs change). Security: RAG OR fine-tune both keep internal data in-house IF GLM is self-hosted (air-gapped) — NEVER send internal DB/wiki to the China API. Pipeline: wiki → embed → vectorDB → retrieve top-k → GLM answers with citations.

children.name: enterprise-large-corp-deployment
children.summary: Design for a Samsung-class enterprise (Samsung Electronics = semiconductor trade secrets; Samsung Biologics = GMP/FDA-regulated CDMO). At this conservatism tier, model CHOICE matters less than ISOLATION + governance, and the China model (GLM) is excluded on reputational/regulatory grounds even though self-hosting would technically contain the data. Researched 2026-06-22; internal-analysis.

children.name: model-selection
children.summary: 3 candidate classes: (1) China open (GLM-5.2) — EXCLUDED for Samsung-class: US House inquiry target, censorship/jailbreak concerns, reputational risk; self-hosting contains data but political/optics burden remains. (2) Western open-weight (Gemma/Llama) — TOP PICK: clean license + politics, easy self-host, reputationally safe. (3) Closed enterprise (Azure OpenAI / Bedrock Claude, KR/private region) — clear liability+SLA but data leaves the boundary. Verdict: Western open-weight self-hosted is the default for trade-secret environments.

children.name: model-size-note
children.summary: Gemma standard sizes are 12B / 27B (user's '24b' ≈ 27B confusion). Size is set by USE: internal wiki/DB Q&A via RAG → mid-size 12-27B is plenty (retrieval supplies the facts, big model unnecessary), fits a single H100 → far easier ops. Complex coding/agentic reasoning → large 70B+. Bio domain reasoning (papers/experiments) → large + domain fine-tune. NOTE: confirm exact current Gemma/Llama lineup + per-size VRAM + license before committing (not re-verified this session).

children.name: architecture
children.summary: Air-gapped/zero-egress VPC or on-prem (e.g. DGX): [Gemma 27B self-host via vLLM, single H100] + [vector DB indexing internal wiki/DB → RAG] + [gateway: SSO·RBAC·audit-log·DLP output filter·prompt logging]. Internet egress = 0. China API = forbidden. Knowledge via RAG (citations/freshness), NOT fine-tuning. Controls layer: SSO, RBAC, audit log, DLP output filter, prompt/response logging.

children.name: samsung-electronics-vs-biologics
children.summary: Samsung Electronics (semiconductor): design/process trade secrets → air-gap + internal-code RAG; coding/doc assistance focus. Samsung Biologics (CDMO): adds GMP + FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — when AI output touches quality/regulatory docs it incurs validation + audit-trail + data-integrity obligations → more conservative, MANDATORY human final review; AI is assist-only, never the system of record.

children.name: inference-performance
children.summary: Single-request token-generation speed (tok/s), hardware fit, and the MoE-quant vs dense-70B trade. All tok/s are ESTIMATES/feel, not benchmarked. Researched 2026-06-22; internal-analysis.

children.name: speed-vs-claude-code
children.summary: Question: 'Claude Code급 속도?' — separate 3 axes: SPEED(tok/s) vs CAPABILITY(intelligence) vs CONCURRENCY(simultaneous users). SPEED only, single-user: Gemma 27B @ 1xH100 ~40-80 tok/s (BF16 ~40-50, FP8/opt ~60-80) ≈ or faster than Claude Sonnet (~50-100) / faster than Opus (~30-60); all >> human read ~10-15. Local TTFT also faster (no network round-trip). BUT 'Claude Code급' as CAPABILITY ≠ speed: 27B << Opus (Claude Code's real engine = large frontier model + agent harness), so for complex multi-file refactor/long reasoning the gap is large → need 70B+/large or GLM. CONCURRENCY: 1xH100 throughput is fixed → many simultaneous users split it, per-user tok/s drops; hundreds of users need multi-GPU.

children.name: 70b-speed-and-hw
children.summary: 70B single-request ~15-30 tok/s (slower than 27B, still > human read). Q4 ~20-40. Memory vs 1xH100(80GB): BF16 ~140GB → NOT 1 GPU, needs 2; FP8 ~70GB → tight 1 GPU (low KV/context headroom); Q4 ~40GB → 1 GPU OK. So 70B on 1xH100 needs FP8(tight) or Q4(roomy); full BF16 / long-context / multi-user → 2 GPU. Capability one tier above 27B (Sonnet-近접) but still below Claude Opus.

children.name: glm-quant-vs-dense-70b
children.summary: KEY PARADOX (MoE 'big brain, small compute' vs dense 'mid brain, full compute'): GLM-5.2 = 744B total but only ~40B ACTIVE per token. So vs dense 70B: (memory) GLM-2bit 238GB > 70B 140GB — GLM BIGGER; (compute/speed) GLM active-40B > 70B full-70B — GLM FASTER; (capability) GLM 744B-brain > 70B — GLM SMARTER. 3-way: GLM-5.2 Q4 (~400GB, 4xH200, active-40B fast, 744B capability near-kept) | GLM-5.2 2bit (~238GB, 2xH200, fast, capability DAMAGED) | 70B FP8 (~70GB, 1xH100, slow, dense-70B). Verdict: GPU-rich(4xH200+) → GLM Q4 beats 70B on BOTH capability & speed; GPU-tight(1xH100) → 70B (GLM won't fit); GPU-mid(2xH200) → awkward, GLM-2bit damaged so prefer 70B or GLM hosting. 70B's ONLY edge = fits 1xH100 (memory efficiency). AVOID GLM-2bit: bigger than 70B AND quality-degraded.
